Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask for dedicated migration (RDW-3491)

Laura — appreciated, received the CSV and reviewed offline with infra. Attached is a first-pass phased-onboard-matrix.xlsx that maps traffic slices to GPU shard counts, warmup windows, and verification gates. Summary of our proposal: 

Phase A (staging validation, 3 days)
- Mirrored traffic (non-prod) for 48h to confirm kernel/sequence performance
- 24h smoke with synthetic traffic to validate latency SLOs (<120ms p95 on chat)
- Alloc: 8xA100-equivalent GPUs (multi-tenant pool replica)

Phase B (gradual traffic ramp, 5 days)
- Canary at 5–10% of production traffic → increase in 2x steps every 24h
- KV cache warmup & prefix-caching enabled at step 2
- Alloc: scale to 24xA100-equivalent GPUs by final ramp step

Phase C (commit & blackbox acceptance)
- Final 24h acceptance run at 100% routed to dedicated pool
- Ops rollback window 2 hours post-cutover

We can do mirrored+smoke to minimize disruption; the 48h stress window is optional if you’re comfortable with a longer mirrored period (we usually prefer one high-load stress window to exercise failure modes).

Regarding compressing schedule: we can shave one week by overlapping Phase A and B preparatory tasks (start mirror while pre-warming KV caches), which would land us in production the weekend of Sep 2–3. That still gives you one week buffer before your Sep 8 board demo. I’ll mark the Aug 22–23 blackout in the timeline and avoid any heavy ops then.

Attachments: phased-onboard-matrix.xlsx, commitment-terms-draft.pdf

Links: HubSpot RDW-3491, shared Drive folder with runbooks (see links below).

Proposed next call: Thu Aug 12 10:00 PT to lock the schedule and DocuSign scope. Does that work?

Best,
Neha
--

Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-08-11T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Phased onboard & sizing matrix — technical notes

Laura/Team — quick technical notes to add context to the matrix (keeps the acceptance window tight):
- Kernel selection: given 780-token p95s we’ll pin to the long-seq kernel path; expect ~12–18% higher GPU cycles than baseline short-seq runs. We accounted for this in the matrix.
- KV cache warmup: recommend a 36–48h warmup prior to routing live traffic; we will seed from a mirror of recent sessions to avoid initial cold penalties.
- Batching & concurrency: we’ll start on conservative batching (target latency SLOs) and progressively enable continuous-batching once latency stabilizes. That’s part of Phase B step 2.
- Stress test: if you want to avoid a 48h destructive stress window, we can do a 72h mirror + 12h synthetic high-QPS ramp that hits the same failure curves but without injecting faults.

Operationally we’ll need a single point-of-contact for day-of cutover (for roll/rollback calls) and an on-call list (we’ve added platform@echelonhealth.com as primary).

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
